questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Rims with a missing lug nut are acceptable if at least four other lug nuts are present.
A cracked lock ring is acceptable if you drive under 55 mph.
A missing clamp is dangerous and must be fixed.
Welded repairs are acceptable for rear axle wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp is dangerous and must be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lugs are dangerous defects. Mismatched, bent, or cracked lock rings are not safe. Welded wheels or rims are not safe.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe play on a 20-inch steering wheel?
questions.explanation: A steering wheel with more than 10 degrees of play may be defective. On a 20-inch wheel, this equals about two inches of movement at the rim.

questions.question: What should you always do when approaching a railroad crossing with a placarded vehicle?

options.text: Stop within five feet of the tracks.
Change gears while on the tracks.
Change lanes while on the tracks.

questions.explanation: Before crossing railroad tracks with a placarded vehicle, stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail. Turn on your four-way flashers while crossing. Do not stop, change gears, or change lanes while crossing the tracks.

questions.question: What should you do with your mirrors while driving?

options.text: Do not use them because they are distracting.
Use them only when there is traffic.
Check them regularly, but only on cloudy days.

questions.explanation: You must stay aware of your surroundings at all times. Check your mirrors regularly.

questions.question: What can happen if you press and release the brake pedal unnecessarily?

options.text: Air is released faster than the compressor can replace it.
More air is added to the brake system.
The brake pedal becomes harder to push.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air is released faster than the compressor can replace it.
questions.explanation: On vehicles with air brakes, pressing and releasing the brake pedal unnecessarily releases air from the system faster than the compressor can replace it. This can cause air pressure to drop too low and the brakes to fail.

questions.question: What should you do when parked on the side of a road?

options.text: Stand in the road and wave your arms.

questions.explanation: If you must stop on the roadside, turn on your emergency flashers to alert other drivers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: What should you do if you must drive very slowly?
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly, warn drivers behind you by turning on your emergency flashers, as long as local law allows it.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel when driving?

options.text: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
With both hands at the bottom of the wheel.
With both hands at the top of the wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: Where should your vehicle's final position be?

options.text: Within five feet of the examiner's final position.
Within two feet of the examiner's final position.

questions.explanation: You must park your vehicle in the exact position the examiner describes. Failure to do so exactly may result in penalties or failure of the basic control skills test.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a double combination vehicle during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: You must know the maximum safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A double combination vehicle must not lose more than 4 psi per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights. Do this even during the day.

questions.question: What should you do with the stairwell of a bus?

options.text: Use it to store items if needed.
Use it as a seat if needed.
Use it to store small items.
Keep it clear at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it clear at all times.
questions.explanation: The aisles and stairwell of a bus must always be kept clear. Do not allow passengers to store bags or items in these areas.

questions.question: During a steering box inspection, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Check that the steering box is securely mounted.
Check that the steering box has no leaks.
Look for missing bolts in the steering box.
Assume all cotter keys are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume all cotter keys are present.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check that the steering box is securely mounted. Look for missing nuts, bolts, and cotter keys. Check for power steering fluid leaks and damage to hoses.

questions.question: What can help you know when to shift to a higher gear?
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift up. First is engine speed (rpm). Check your manual to learn the correct rpm range and shift up when you reach the top. Second is road speed (mph). Learn which speeds work for each gear, watch your speedometer, and shift up as needed.

questions.question: If a school bus must be evacuated, what should passengers do?
questions.explanation: In an emergency, the driver must quickly decide which exit is safest and direct passengers to use it.

questions.question: When driving a 50-foot truck at 50 mph, what is the minimum following distance?
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, keep at least one second of distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length. At higher speeds, add one more second.

questions.question: How can you avoid blocking traffic when driving a heavy vehicle?

options.text: Try to pass other vehicles while driving uphill.
Ride the brakes while driving downhill.

questions.explanation: If your heavy vehicle cannot match traffic speed, stay in the right lane when possible.

questions.question: What should properly adjusted outside side flat mirrors show on a school bus?

options.text: The sides of the school bus
The front tires touching the ground
Vehicles in front of the bus

questions.correctAnswerText: The sides of the school bus
questions.explanation: When properly adjusted, outside side flat mirrors should show the sides of the bus, the rear tires on the ground, and 200 feet behind the bus.

questions.question: Which item is required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: All commercial vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or three flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: If you stop on the road or shoulder, what must you do within 10 minutes?

options.text: Stand behind your vehicle and signal traffic to pass.

questions.explanation: When stopped on the road or shoulder, place emergency warning devices like reflective triangles within 10 minutes.
